subject.title: Feishu: duplicate final replies can occur after model failover from rate-limited primary

question: Should OpenClaw treat an errored primary attempt plus recovered fallback as one user-visible Feishu final, and should the guard live in Feishu streaming closeout, shared final-dispatch identity, or the broader durable delivery contract?
rationale: Current code intentionally preserves some later finals after errors, so an automated fix could either suppress useful diagnostics or leave the duplicate-failover path unresolved without maintainer intent.

options.title: Narrow Feishu recovery guard
options.body: Make Feishu keep or replace the errored-attempt card during transient failure and deliver only the recovered fallback final for the user turn, with explicit exceptions for distinct diagnostics.

options.title: Shared final identity contract
options.body: Define a dispatcher-level same-turn final identity so all channels collapse failed-attempt/recovered-fallback duplicates while preserving intentionally distinct finals.

options.title: Fold into durable delivery roadmap
options.body: Track this only under the broader durable final-delivery contract and defer a Feishu-local fix until that contract is designed.

recommendation.title: Narrow Feishu recovery guard
recommendation.body: Make Feishu keep or replace the errored-attempt card during transient failure and deliver only the recovered fallback final for the user turn, with explicit exceptions for distinct diagnostics.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest recent merged history in the Feishu error-final dispatcher surface and adjacent review context.
